Commentary.Commentary: That's it from this match. Australia Women continue to rule the roost and head the table with four consecutive wins. Up next is a battle of survival on Wednesday, 16th March 2022. The reigning champions have their title defense on the line after suffering three consecutive losses. They take on buoyant India Women at Bay Oval, Mount Maunganui and another defeat will push England Women to the brink of an early exit. The first ball will be at 6.30 am IST (1 am GMT) but you can join us in advance for the build-up. Cheers!

Meg Lanning, the victorious captain of Australia Women, says that it's all about adjusting to the breeze here and assessing the conditions well. Adds that they are blessed to have such good depth in the squad that anyone can come in and perform at the highest level. She adds that Rachael Haynes and Beth Mooney batted really well but also adds that they don't want to lose early wickets. Smiles and rates their batting performance as 7 out of 10. Mentions that the Windies had a clear plan when they came out to bowl and that made it a bit difficult. About moving to Auckland for the next game, Meg replies that it should be fun against India and they are ready for it.

Stafanie Taylor, the captain of West Indies Women, says that it was not the best batting display from them. Adds that they pride themselves on their batting and admits that they didn't assess the conditions well and lost too many wickets upfront. Shares that they were aiming for a score above 250. Tells that 130 was way below par but her bowling group did really well. Mentions that they still have 3 more games and have to leave this game behind and move on. She is happy with her personal form.

Ellyse Perry (8-0-22-3) is chosen for the Player of the Match award! She also played a handy supporting role in a crucial stand with Rachael Haynes. Perry says that the conditions were nice to bowl early on with the slope and she got wickets as well so she is happy. Adds that she is trying to work on her shape with the new ball and trying out variations and the more she bowls before the match, the better control she has. Mentions that sometimes Test matches help you to get into a rhythm as you get to bowl more. Adds that the conditions here have been different due to the breeze and they like playing here.
Presentation time...

Earlier in the day, the match started after a delay of 30 minutes due to rain. There was a tinge of green on the surface and coupled with the overcast conditions, it was perfect for bowling. However, Stafanie Taylor decided to bat first. They were pegged back thrice inside Powerplay 1 by Ellyse Perry and never recovered. The Aussie spinners also choked the flow of runs and suffocated West Indies Women for runs. Only Stafanie Taylor managed to score some runs as the rest just surrendered. Two hefty defeats for them now and they need to find a way out from this losing rut.

A target of 132 would have never challenged the batting powerhouse of Australia Women. Although they were rocked early by Hayley Matthews, they knew one good partnership will be enough to see them through. They ended up getting two with Rachael Haynes being the common participant in both. With Ellyse Perry, she added 51 runs to steady the ship after early hiccups and then with Beth Mooney, Haynes made sure to complete the task with 118 balls to spare.

Comfortable win for Australia Women but they had to work hard in the chase. The scorecard won't tell you the entire story. It was an abysmal batting show by West Indies Women which disallowed them to get a challenging total on the board otherwise this match had all the ingredients to be a cracker. The kind of intensity shown in the field by the Caribbean team was brilliant and they really pushed the Aussies hard.

That's it! It's all over. A high full toss, on middle. Rachael Haynes steps out and pulls it towards deep mid-wicket for a single to finish things off. What a knock it has been from her! Australia Women win by 7 wickets!
Floated up, right in the blockhole. Haynes jams it out on the off side.
Around middle and leg, flicked away straight to mid-wicket and there's no run there.

A bit of width on offer and Haynes steers it to the left of deep backward point. The batters look for two but Chinelle Henry is quick to get across and keeps it down to a single. The scores are now level.
Pitched up, on middle, Haynes stays solid in defense.
Around the top of off, played behind point for a single.
FOUR! Impeccable from Beth Mooney! An inviting half-volley on off, Mooney caresses it through covers for a glorious boundary. Just 3 required now.
Back of a length, on the leg stump line, Mooney steps out and dabs it down towards backward point.
Flatter delivery, around middle. This is pushed towards mid on.
FOUR! Another full toss, on middle. Rachael Haynes steps out and slogs it away, one bounce into the mid-wicket fence for a boundary.
Beth Mooney almost cleans up Rachael Haynes at the non-striker's end! A juicy full toss, it's thumped down towards long on for a single.
Down the leg side, swept away past short fine leg. Just as Haynes looks to turn back for the second, she slips and it will only be a single.
Taylor sees Mooney advancing and slides it down leg. Mooney does manage to sweep it away to deep backward square leg for a single.
Floated up, very full and on middle, Mooney blocks it out.
Banged in short and outside off. Rachael Haynes gets on top of the bounce and slaps it towards deep backward point. The batters push hard for two and have done a great job.
Length ball, around off. This is tapped towards cover-point.
And again! Slower this time, Selman rolls her fingers over the ball and slides it across the off stump. Haynes misses the cut once again.
Nicely bowled! Pitched up in that channel around off. Haynes hangs back and looks to nudge it away. The ball bounces a bit extra and goes over the blade.
Around the top of off, guided down to third man for a run.
On off, Mooney walks down the track and punches it towards deep cover. Chedean Nation attacks the ball well but misfields and this allows the batters to come back for the second.
FOUR! Poor delivery! Short and wide, Rachael Haynes waits for it and then cuts it behind point for another boundary. Australia Women just 19 runs away from another victory.
Flatter and darted into off. Haynes keeps it out.

FOUR! Just over! Tossed up on off. Rachael Haynes shimmies down the track but doesn't quite get to the pitch of the ball. She still goes through with the lofted shot and just about clears Stafanie Taylor at mid off. The ball runs away into the fence and the 50 partnership is up between these two.
Around middle and leg, Mooney steps out and flicks it through square leg for one more.
Slower through the air, angled into middle and Haynes is pushed onto the back foot. Haynes nudges it out on the off side and sneaks in a single.
Sliding down leg, paddled away straight to the fielder at short fine leg.
Shamilia Connell has hurt herself after the last fielding attempt. She is limping off. Cherry-Ann Fraser comes out as a substitute fielder.
Around the top of off, tapped towards the cover region where Shamilia Connell tries to collect the ball with a slide and has injured herself. Just 29 needed more.
Back of a length, around off. Haynes opens the face of the blade and steers it down to third man for a single.
Full and wide, Beth Mooney makes a bit of room, steps out and mistimes the cover drive. Connell slips though and allows the batters to take the single.
Good-length, over middle, Mooney defends it right under her eye line and towards point.
Full and around off, Mooney looks to cream it through covers but mistimes it to Shamilia Connell at extra cover.
Slower and shorter, on off. Rachael Haynes hangs back and pulls it down to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Skidding down the leg side, Mooney fails to properly middle her sweep shot. 10 from the over, 32 needed more.
FOUR! Superb shot! Full and floated around off, Beth Mooney shimmies down the track and cracks it through covers for a boundary. 100 up!
Beaten! Turn and bounce around off, Beth Mooney hangs behind to push inside the line and is beaten.

PUT DOWN! Loopy and full on middle, some extra bounce, Rachael Haynes goes down to sweep but it takes the top edge and flies to short fine leg. Shakera Selman thinks that it will go over her so she starts to turn but then realizes that the ball has swung towards her right and there is a chance to catch it. She sticks her right hand up but it brushes her palm and deflects away. A single is taken.
FOUR! Fantastic footwork from Rachael Haynes. She walks down to the pitch of the delivery and lofts a full ball just over mid off. Once the ball lands, it has enough wheels to get to the fence.
Full and outside off, driven through covers for one.
Hayley Matthews (6-2-11-1) is brought back in a desperate attempt to break the partnership.

Risky single. Fractionally short in length and around off, Mooney dabs it to point and scampers across to the other end. Deandra Dottin misses her shy at the bowler's end otherwise Mooney could have been out.
On a length around off, Mooney looks to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads. It deflects to point, Beth looks for a run but is sent back.
Slower in pace, outside off, played down to point.
Full again, outside off, Haynes strokes it to sweeper cover for one.
Fuller and around off, driven to mid off for a single.

COLLISION! Two players down, hopefully, nothing serious. A touch short in length, close to off, Rachael Haynes defends it down off the inner half and the ball rests near the popping crease. They decide to steal a run and Shemaine Campbelle, the keeper, rushes forward. She tries to pick up the ball and back flick it onto the stumps but misses. Meanwhile, Beth Mooney comes running in, gets to the crease and nearly knees down Shemaine Campbelle. There is a collision but only a slight one. Campbelle has hurt her shoulders but is fine to continue. FYI... a direct hit would have found Beth short of the crease.
On middle and leg, tucked behind square leg for a run. 46 needed more.
Full and floated around off, Beth takes a step down and drives it on the up. It's aerial but in the gap through covers for a single.
Loopy and full around off, Mooney steps down the track a bit and bunts it to mid on.
Short again and outside off, this time Haynes cuts it past the diving point fielder for a single.
Short in length and outside off, Rachael Haynes cuts but finds the point fielder.
Advances down the track to a full ball and drills it past the bowler. Finds mid off though.
Taps a length ball down to cover-point for a single. Under 50 needed now.
Around off, slightly on a fuller length and angling away, Haynes presses forward and pushes it to point.
Back of a length, around middle, Haynes rocks back and defends it on the leg side.
FOUR! Yet another fifty for Rachael Haynes, her 17th in ODIs and 4th in World Cups. Short in length, around middle and leg, Haynes swivels and nails her pull shot behind square leg for a boundary.
Overpitches, around off, Moone strokes it with great timing and the ball races away. The mid off fielder does well to make the stop but cannot prevent the single.
Fractionally short and on top of off, Beth Mooney stands tall and taps it down on the off side. She sets off for a run but is sent back.
Short again, outside off, cut behind point for two.
Wide! Quicker one, short and wide outside off, Haynes leaves. 10 from the over, 55 needed more.
Use of the feet again, this time from Rachael Haynes. She skips down the track to a full ball outside off and lifts it over mid off for a couple.
Short and wide outside off, cut to point where the fielder misfields and allows a run.
Fuller and around off, angled in, it's defended back to the bowler.
FOUR! Enough is enough! Beth Mooney uses her feet to dance down to the pitch of the ball and lofts it over mid on for a boundary.
Full and flighted outside off, driven through the line but finds the point fielder.
Pitched up on off. Haynes pushes it out towards covers. Australia Women need 65 more runs off 180 balls. It's all about the wickets now for West Indies Women.
Good-length, slanting across off. Mooney taps it towards point where Deandra Dottin misfields and allows the batters to cross over.
Full and straight, dug out on the off side for a quick single.
This is banged into the body but the ball doesn't rise up much. Haynes is through her pull early and gets a blow into the midriff.
Nicely driven but straight to the fielder. Full, around off and Haynes can't pierce the inner ring on the off side.
Pitched up around middle and leg. Rachael Haynes plays a solid front foot defensive shot.
On off, driven towards covers.
Flatter this time, worked towards point.
Loopt delivery, around off. Mooney uses her feet and then turns it into a low full toss but can't get it through the cover region.
Sliding into middle, pushed towards mid off.
Very full and outside off. Rachael Haynes reaches out and laps it through backward square leg for a single.
Slower through the air, angled into middle. Haynes steps out and makes a block.
This is slanted across off. Beth Mooney opens the face of the bat and times it well but can't get it past Deandra Dottin at point.
On middle and leg, pushed towards short mid-wicket.
Full and around off, Haynes opens the face of the bat and guides it down to third man for yet another single.
Fuller in length, on off. Mooney eases it towards covers for one.
Leg bye! Down the leg side, Haynes misses the tuck. The ball goes off the pads and rolls towards short fine leg. They get a leg bye.

Excellent fielding again from Chedean Nation and she saves a certain boundary. Length ball, outside off. Rachael Haynes stands tall and strokes it behind point. Nation runs in from the point fence and puts in the dive to keep it down to a couple of runs.
A hint of flight on this one. Around off and Mooney caresses it to the cover region. Just the one run off the over.
Tossed up around off, Mooney with a gentle push towards covers.
Full again, floated on off. Mooney keeps it out towards the bowler.
Full and on off. Blocked out.
Drop and run. Floated and around off, Haynes plays it with gentle hands to cover-point for a single.
Fuller and on off, driven back to the bowler off the inner half.
Beth Mooney is the new batter.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! Chinelle Henry gets the big wicket of Ellyse Perry and West Indies Women are still in this match. Fullish ball, on a driving length and around off. Ellyse Perry reaches for it as she looks to drive but gets the outside edge. The ball flies to first slip where who else but Hayley Matthews takes another sharp catch. Brilliant from Matthews and Henry gets her first wicket of the day.
Commentary.Howout: c Hayley Matthews b Chinelle Henry

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length, around off. Haynes steers it down to third man for a single.
A length ball, around off. This is tapped towards backward point.
FOUR! Short ball, down the leg side. Rachael Haynes pulls it really fine and beats the fielder at fine leg. Welcome boundary for Haynes.

Rachael Haynes has broken her bat and needs a change. Meanwhile, the umpires have decided to call for Drinks also. In a simple chase, Australia Women were rocked early by the brilliance of Hayley Matthews but the current stand has kept the match firmly in the favour of the Aussies. West Indies Women have been all charged up in the field and trying their best. Let's see how they perform in the middle phase. 79 more needed for a win.

Huge mix up in the middle but Rachael Haynes survives! Good-length around middle and leg and nipping in. Haynes looks to flick it on the leg side but the ball comes off the shoulder of the bat and hits her on the thigh pad. A part of the bat comes off and Haynes wants the single. She is halfway through when she is sent back and Chinelle Henry does well to attack the ball but she misses the direct hit at the keeper's end. Had she hit, Haynes was a goner.
Touch fuller, on a nagging length and slanted across the left-hander. Haynes looks to drive but gets beaten past the outside edge.
Goes on the back foot to a short ball and helps it to mid-wicket. Tidy over!
A touch short and outside off, this time Haynes plays it to the right of Shakera Selman at covers for a single.
Well stopped by Selman! Around off, Rachael Haynes forces it through the line but Shakera Selman throws herself to right and stops the ball with a full-length dive.
Wide! Another one down the leg side, Haynes fails to make any use of it.
Wide! Down the leg side, Rachael tries to sweep but misses.
Edged but safe! Loopy and full around off, turning away, Rachael Haynes gets forward to defend it with an angled bat but gets a soft outside edge. It falls short of Hayley Matthews at first slip.
Loopy and full around off, defended to the off side.
A touch short and on middle, Perry goes on the back foot and works it through mid-wicket for a single.
This one has been stroked to point. The fielder fumbles slightly but no run taken.
Outside off, played down to covers.

Chinelle Henry continues to serve on a fuller length outside off, Ellyse Perry drives it with good timing and the extra cover fielder makes only a half stop. The mid off fielder cuts it off and they cross.
Full again, outside off, this time to a left-hander, Haynes caresses it to sweeper cover for one.
Fullish and outside off, Perry drills it through covers for a single.
Starts with a full ball on middle, Ellyse Perry brings down a straight bat and pushes it towards mid on.
Chinelle Henry comes in to replace Shamilia Connell.
Play and a miss! Full and wide outside off, Rachael Haynes tries to sweep but fails to connect.
Flighted one, full and on off, Rachael Haynes draws forward and brings her bat and pad together in defense.
Loopy delivery, full and around off, Haynes defends it with gentle hands to covers.
Short and wide outside off, punched through covers for one.
Short in length around off, Perry goes back and drags her attempted pull shot to short mid-wicket.
Flighted delivery, full and around off, Haynes drives it through covers for a single.
Here comes the first bowling change as Karishma Ramharack is brought into the attack.
On middle and leg, it's tucked behind square leg for a run. 88 needed more!
Another wide! This time Shamilia Connell delivers it way wide outside off, on a length. Haynes leaves.
Wide! Short but down the leg side, left alone.
Fuller and on middle, skidding off the surface, Ellyse Perry tries to flick but closes the face of her bat early. It bobbles out off the leading edge but goes through the gap at covers for a run.
Around off, played down to cover-point for a single.
Short and wide outside off, Ellyse Perry reaches out and cuts it past the point fielder for a single. A bit of a misfield inside the ring.
Once again lands it very full and off, this time to Perry who pushes it down to mid off.
Pitches it up and outside off, Rachael Haynes drives it through the gap at covers for one.
Loopy and full outside off, Perry presses forward and drives it to mid off.
Fullish and down the leg side, Haynes goes down and sweeps it wide of short fine leg for a run.
Fires it flat and short around off, Haynes stays back and plays it down to point.
Fuller and around off, Rachael Haynes strokes it through cover-point for a couple of runs.
Sliding down the leg side, Haynes plays late at it but finds the short fine leg fielder.
A touch short in length around middle, Ellyse Perry goes on the back foot and turns it in front of square on the leg side for a single.
Powerplay 2 time. A maximum of 4 fielders are now allowed outside the ring till the 40th over, if the match lasts till then.
Good-length, over middle. Haynes hops to defend. At the end of the first Powerplay, Australia Women are 33/2!
Excellent delivery! Connell delivers a toe-crushing yorker and Ellyse Perry does well to jam it out. The batters scamper through for a run as well as the ball rolls behind square leg.
Fuller in length, around off. Rachael Haynes stays in her crease and caresses it towards deep cover for a single. She looks for two but decides against it.
Pitched up, on middle. Haynes punches it back towards the bowler who gets a hand on it.
This is banged into the deck. Haynes defends it off the back foot.
A length ball, slanting across the left-hander. Haynes taps it towards point.
On middle, driven straight to mid on. Maiden!
Tossed up, on off and this is eased towards mid off.
Around off again, played towards the point region.
Flatter this time, around off. Perry rocks back and cuts it to point.
Quicker delivery, fuller and outside off. Ellyse Perry makes a watchful leave.
On middle, this is pushed towards mid on.
A length ball, angled across the off stump. Left alone by Haynes.
FOUR! Just a fraction short and Rachael Haynes latches onto it. This is on the leg stump line and Haynes pulls it behind square on the leg side for a boundary.
And again! Fullish ball, outside off and this is stroked away towards sweeper cover for two more.
Full and wide again, this time Haynes drives it through the cover region for a couple of runs.
Full and wide, Haynes doesn't play at it.

NOT OUT! Excellent review from Rachael Haynes and she survives. This is a length ball, pitching around the leg stump and angling across the left-hander. Haynes gets caught on the crease and misses the flick. She gets pinged on the back leg and Shamilia Connell runs away in celebration. The umpire gives it out but Haynes reviews after consulting her partner. UltraEdge shows there's no bat involved and Ball Tracking shows that the ball was just missing the top of the middle stump. The onfield decision has been overturned.

The finger goes up! Rachael Haynes is gone lbw but she wants to review the decision. Flat line as the ball goes past the bat, confirms the UltraEdge. Ball Tracking - Pitching in line, hitting in line...but missing the stumps. Haynes survives.
Flatter delivery, outside off and this is slapped towards covers.
Flatter delivery, around off. Perry leaves it alone.
Quicker, on off. This is pulled down towards mid on.
Tossed up full and on the stumps. Haynes paddles it towards fine leg for a run.
Around off, pushed towards covers.

Shout for an lbw! Not given and DRS is taken. It really was a hopeful review from Stafanie Taylor. This is on a full length, around off and angling in. Rachael Haynes puts a big stride forward and outside off stump and looks to get inside the line of the ball. She misses the paddle and gets rapped on the pads. Shout for an lbw, not given! DRS taken. The impact looked outside off. UltraEdge finds no wood and Ball Tracking confirms that the impact was well outside off
Short and wide again, played off the back foot behind point for a single.
WIDE! This is spilled down the leg side. Wided.
FOUR! Top shot and with this boundary Rachael Haynes becomes the top-scorer of the tournament. Short and wide, Haynes hangs back and just glides it behind point with exquisite timing for a boundary.
Back of a length, there's a bit of width on offer. Haynes thrashes it to point.
FOUR! Not timed perfectly but it's in the gap! Short ball, around leg. Rachael Haynes gets in position early and pulls it well in front of square on the leg side for a welcome boundary.
On off again, Haynes nudges it out towards covers with soft hands.
A length ball on off. Haynes hangs back and taps it towards cover-point.
Around off, kept out on the off side.
Quicker and flatter, close to the off stump. Ellyse Perry cuts it hard but straight towards cover-point.
Flatter ball, on off. Perry hops back to defend.
On off, Perry drives it firmly to mid off.
Sliding down leg again and paddled away towards fine leg for just a single this time.
On a length, sliding onto leg stump. Rachael Haynes gets low and gets inside the line of the ball to lap it towards fine leg for a couple of runs.
Shortish and on off, played down from the back foot to covers.
Short and wide outside off, Ellyse whacks it through the line but the point fielder makes a diving stop.
Outside off, left alone.
Short and wide outside off, slapped through point for a couple of runs.

OUT! CAUGHT AT FIRST SLIP! West Indies Women are turning on the heat and once again Hayley Matthews has taken a sensational catch. The delivery is on the shorter side, plenty of width available and Meg Lanning goes chasing after it. She throws her bat at it but only to get a thick outside edge. It flies to first slip at the rate of knots but Matthews is equally up to the challenge. She sticks her hands up and snaps a tremendous reflex catch just over her head. Ellyse Perry has walked in next with Australia Women in early trouble.
Commentary.Howout: c Hayley Matthews b Shamilia Connell

Commentary.Commentary: Shortish and on off, played down on the leg side.
Skidding in from around middle, Haynes tries to work it on the leg side but misses. Takes a blow high on the front leg.
Spinning down the leg side, Meg fails to flick and it goes off her pads to short fine leg. They take a leg bye.
Tossed up, outside off, pushed gently to point.
Loopy and full around off, defended off the front foot.
Well stopped! West Indies Women showing great energy in the field. A full toss around off, Meg Lanning crunches it to covers where Chedean Nation dives across to her left to stop the racing ball.
The skipper, Meg Lanning walks out to bat at number 3.

OUT! CAUGHT AND BOWLED! Great reaction and it's a fantastic return catch. That came back like a rocket. Full and floated around off, Alyssa Healy is not to the pitch of the ball and smacks it straight back. Hayley Matthews reverse cups it close to her heart and goes down to complete the catch. Just the kind of start West Indies Women needed. Can they build on it?
In the channel outside off, on a length and angling away, Rachael Haynes has nothing to do with it.
Fullish and outside off, Healy reaches out and strokes it through covers for a single.
Slants in a length ball on middle, Alyssa Healy covers the line and defends it back.
Width there outside off, short in length, Haynes cracks it past backward point. The third man is standing quite square and hence only a run.
Angles across a length ball, around off, Rachael Haynes covers her stumps and shoulders arms.
Shamilia Connell begins with a shortish delivery around off, Healy stands back and taps it down to cover-point for a run.
Shamilia Connell to steam in from the opposite end.
A bit edgy but in control. Tossed up, full and around off, Rachael Haynes strides forward and plays late with an angled bat. It takes the outer half and races past short third man for a couple.
Beaten on the drive! Grip and turn for Hayley Matthews as she lands it on a fuller length outside off, Rachael Haynes attempts to drive but misses.
Slow spin back into the batter from around off, on a fuller length, Alyssa Healy plays nice and late as he helps it behind square leg for a single. Australia Women are underway!
Presses forward to a full ball and pushes it softly to point.
Loopy and full, around off, Alyssa Healy gets on the front foot and defends it to the off side.
Flighted and full, around middle, Healy flicks it across the line but finds the diving mid-wicket fielder.
